rulings: Ruling: Existing linked worktree is reused and no host dependency install/full unbounded suite is run — explicit approved plan preserves isolation and names proportional seventeen-file gate, overriding generic skill defaults — cost if wrong: unrelated broad failures remain outside this increment and must not be described as green.

Task1: Ruling: Bring the test-only fixture-root change forward from Task4 — source native tests must never recreate the deleted predecessor scratch; accept only this exact plan root and its relative or exact MSYS marker — cost if wrong: a required native harness blocks before fixtures, no runtime authority.

Task1: Ruling: Keep full128-bit random fixture IDs in a shorter base64url test directory name — Git worktree registration returned fatal GIT_DIR too big at the longer new-plan scratch path; core.longpaths did not fix the registration limit and was reverted — cost if wrong: synthetic fixture creation fails, no source/runtime scope changes.

Task1: Ruling: Prepare shares the existing-workspace lease for its final proof; OpenExisting already revalidates so remove a duplicate immediate validation — config smoke checks actual prepared HEAD and at least one safe HEAD read, retaining zero reads for malicious config — cost if wrong: redundant work may return, unsafe config still must stop before HEAD. Old exact single-read assertion failed after new validation was introduced.

Task2: Ruling: One fixed suite means one selected test file; Vitest2 counts nested describe groups in numTotalTestSuites — accept positive matching passed-group counts with exactly one testResults file and every test passed — cost if wrong: nested groups could be miscounted, but skipped/failed/empty assertions still block. Installed JsonReporter source and the new failing nested-group test establish this.

Task2: Ruling: Use two distinct build-owned empty npm config files instead of assigning /dev/null to both config layers — installed @npmcli/config rejects double-loading one path; a read-only isolated CLI characterization failed for one path and passed for two empty files — cost if wrong: dependency setup blocks, no user config or lifecycle permission is added.

Task2: Ruling: Reconcile the CLI argument rejection before issuing the first actual build — the approved pull succeeded but Docker without its bundled Buildx rejected --progress with exit125 before any daemon build; same daemon, only base image added, no new containers/volumes/iid. Temporarily expose only the already installed Docker Inc-signed Buildx binary pinned e97f22ff... in the fresh config; retain original evidence, use a separate once-only receipt, no second pull and no retry after any dispatched/uncertain build — cost if wrong: duplicate build/cache/network work; guard tests reject lost replies, other failures, existing iid or resumed attempts. This repairs the authorized Docker build, gives no job/runtime command authority and installs no tool.

Task2: Ruling: Accept omitted/null/empty Cmd only with the exact fixed Node entrypoint — actual Docker image serialization omits an empty command; the new omitted-Cmd regression failed before the narrow decoder fix — cost if wrong: an unintended command could be accepted; any nonempty or nonarray command still fails.

Task3: Ruling: Persist a reserved attempt before TS helper launch and an immutable started/closed tombstone in source-owned .native/windows-workspace/attempts — the plan requires durable attempt identity and no late restart after cleanup; these are bounded infrastructure records, not a project-file write capability — cost if wrong: an attempt can remain blocked and require operator reconciliation; no duplicate source job is allowed.

Task3: Ruling: Use a named semaphore as the nonblocking current-user attempt mutex — Win32 Mutex ownership is thread-affine across await, semaphore release is not; per-attempt tombstones prevent reuse after process death — cost if wrong: contention blocks an attempt; required guards test concurrent refusal and cross-thread release.

Task3: Ruling: Decode only documented omitted false ReadOnly/NoCopy defaults, while rejecting true flags, nonempty subpaths/driver options and other mount kinds — Moby mount types use omitempty; positive normalization and negative-option tests cover this — cost if wrong: a hidden mount behavior could be accepted; actual root mount/type/source/driver/destination and ownership must still match before upload/start.

Task3: Ruling: Persist the actual backend/daemon/profile/manifest tuple before the first resource mutation and require it for later cleanup — a restarted helper must not report absence from a replacement daemon; the retained-volume regression failed before this binding was wired — cost if wrong: cleanup is conservatively blocked after legitimate host identity changes and needs operator reconciliation, rather than falsely declaring old resources removed.

Task4: Ruling: Required predecessor worktree smoke gets a120s test-process timeout instead of60s — repeated retained-lease audits made the legitimate synthetic config case exceed60s; native production budgets stay fixed — cost if wrong: a hung test consumes up to120s before failing.

Task4: Full gate345/346 in17 files,0pending/0todo; sole actual frozen-image fixture failure preserved. Both typechecks and diff-check0. Task4 remains incomplete; final reviewer not dispatched. Ruling: stop at the explicit consumed one-build allowance and propose a bounded recovery addendum — parent plan requires failures stop without extra build/retry — cost if wrong: delayed fixture availability, no weakened proof.

Recovery: Ruling: Derive each recovery image directly from the already frozen original local image rather than rerun the dependency Dockerfile — this structurally excludes package installation even on a cache miss. Bind an owned localhost-only tag to the exact immutable parent ID, verify before/after, retain tag with the approved image; runtime still enrolls only observed immutable image ID. Cost if wrong: local metadata resolution could fail and consume a bounded build attempt; no fallback pull/install. All original RootFS layers must remain the exact prefix plus one COPY layer, and dependency inventory pin stays unchanged.

Recovery: Ruling: Preserve historical cleanup receipts under their original profile and recheck actual absence with a test-only closed observer bound to their persisted original backend/daemon — changing the enrolled image intentionally changes profile hash, so invoking current runtime cleanup on an old profile would conservatively refuse. The observer never creates/starts/removes Docker resources; missing original records/changed peer/present resources fail. Cost if wrong: an old absence check fails, never execution authority or a claim of current-profile cleanup. Unknown-observer-mode RED observed before helper implementation.

Recovery: Ruling: Reuse one1MiB buffer for sequential synchronous file hashing — before-check took~100s and allocating1MiB for each of86893 files would threaten two checks inside150s work budget. Same byte hashes/inventory, no budget increase; owned12000-file hash performance regression observed RED. Cost if wrong: wrong byte-range reuse would fail unchanged inventory/content comparisons rather than grant success.

Recovery: Ruling: The author's speculative50% Windows hashing microbenchmark target is not a product requirement and was NOT met (6929ms→6383ms for12000 identical516-byte reads); preserve both logs and do not claim halved execution time. Retain the single-buffer implementation as a byte-equivalent allocation refactor; actual Linux before/after inventory and fixed native deadlines decide acceptance. Add chunk-boundary/empty-file hash characterization; no runtime timeout changes. Cost if wrong: the final actual fixture fails within its unchanged deadline and Task4 cannot be marked complete. This corrects the prior performance expectation, not a failing production guard.

Final review F1: Ruling: Accept the escaped/opposite-quote assignment gap as Important and fix it in the trusted native source/publication boundaries, leaving the enrolled frozen runner/image byte-identical. Decode quoted escapes and count decoded UTF16 units for the bounded assignment family; source rejection must precede archive/HTTP, returned DTO and persisted JSON-string diagnostics are rescanned. Malformed diagnostic JSON is withheld. No new image build or source execution is authorized or claimed. Cost if wrong: recognizable secret text could escape; regression cases cover both delimiters, escaped quotes, hex/Unicode escapes and19/20 boundaries, while historical42/42 remains tied to its exact image/profile.

Final review declined1: Ruling: Live admission/claim/fence, real cancellation, model/provider dispatch, patch writes, AI orchestration and UI/CLI/publication remain future unimplemented boundaries; this increment only proves the isolated fixture and absence of activation. Cost if wrong: treating the internal facade as a live authority would permit unreviewed jobs, so no such readiness is claimed.

Final review declined2: Ruling: Arbitrary repositories/commands, multi-host setup and general Node compatibility are outside this deliberately fixed workstation/22-file/one-fixture profile. Existing provisioning artifact remains judged as M1. Cost if wrong: a broader project fails qualification; it must not fall back or select a command.

Final review declined3: Ruling: Exhaustive custom/dynamic credentials and every language encoding are outside bounded detector families; ordinary opposite quotes, escaped delimiters and supported hex/Unicode escapes in the named assignment family are in scope and fixed under F1. Cost if wrong: an unrecognized custom secret could be exported, so no exhaustive secrecy guarantee or general model-context export is claimed.

Final review declined4: Ruling: Trusted owner/admin, kernel, Docker backend and pinned distribution compromise remain underlying trust assumptions; identity/drift enforcement is reviewed, not those implementations. Cost if wrong: compromised trusted infrastructure can invalidate isolation/evidence; qualification is not protection from that threat.

Final review declined5: Ruling: Unrelated whole-repository failures and POSIX behavior beyond preserved boundary/probe regressions are not adjudicated by this Windows17-file gate. Cost if wrong: unrelated functionality may remain broken; all-green product or POSIX claims are forbidden.

Final review declined6: Ruling: No fresh build/source execution/daemon fault experiment is added during final review; read-only review and consumed allowances require retained actual evidence, code tests and fresh absence/source checks instead. Cost if wrong: an untested environmental change can block a later attempt; prior42/42 is historical, not newly reproduced.

Final integration: Ruling: Apply the already approved keep-branch/retained-proof/no-push/no-merge/no-deploy choice instead of asking the generic finishing menu again. Cost if wrong: the verified changes remain local and unintegrated; no live benefit is implied.

independentReview.head: 86cfc2f6dbb34d7e466d0fb315266eac2511c87a
strengths: Immutable Git reads disable replacements, verify blob SHA1/content SHA256 and preserve leases before archive publication.
Closed actual-peer Docker grammar and daemon-bound presence/absence; mutation reconciliation without replay.
Persistent reservations/tombstones/original-peer records prevent concurrent or late starts and false cleanup.
Negative mount/ownership/image/environment/runtime coverage and before/after inventories.
Historical failed and successful evidence are distinguished;42/42 actual tests and352/352 postcommit tests.
No operational consumer outside the internal facade/helper.

important.finding: Assignment detector excludes both quotes regardless of delimiter; opposite quotes and escaped delimiters can split an otherwise qualifying20-character literal and bypass source rejection/log redaction.
important.effect: Selected source could publish a recognizable secret; emitted logs could retain the assignment.
important.recommendation: Bounded delimiter/escape-aware scanning, decoded-length boundary tests, rejection before archive/HTTP and equivalent trusted output-publication protection; preserve honest frozen-image identity.
important.disposition: Fixed in trusted native SourceFixturePolicy, MaterializationContracts output publication and decoded-JSON journal persistence using shared SecretTextPolicy. Frozen runner/image/profile unchanged; three native regression modes observed RED then GREEN.

minor.finding: Original executable Dockerfile/provisioner still reproduces known dependency root-mode mismatch; correction exists separately in recovery recipe.
minor.effect: Future operator may prepare an image which later fails dependency-before. Enrolled corrected image remains valid.
minor.recommendation: Mark/disable historical path or maintain corrected current recipe while retaining original bytes/receipt.
minor.disposition: Deferred under approved material-only final fix policy; no new image build implied.

declined.reason: Unimplemented future authority boundaries; absence of activation was reviewed.
Fixed workstation,source allowlist and fixture; provisioning artifact still assessed asM1.

declined.behavior: Exhaustive custom/dynamic secrets and all language encodings
declined.reason: Bounded detector families promised;F1 is inside the promised family.

declined.behavior: Compromise of trusted owner/admin,OS/kernel,Docker backend,pinned distribution
Unrelated whole-repository failures and POSIX beyond boundary/regression evidence
declined.reason: Named17-file Windows gate cannot establish whole-product health.

declined.behavior: Fresh builds,source execution or daemon fault experiments
declined.reason: Read-only review and consumed allowances;code/test definitions/retained evidence assessed.

independentReview.reviewerAssessment: With fixes: secrecy-boundary F1 should be fixed before technical acceptance; saved42/42 is valid for recorded inputs but does not cover missing literal cases.
independentReview.rootAssessment: F1 repaired and verified in one material fix pass;M1 deferred explicitly. Technical completion applies only to bounded local fixture infrastructure. No reviewer rerun or integration/live approval is claimed.
